The first and highest-frequency tests give affine bounds with slopes -u and v; minimizing their maximum and using the hub budget gives μ(P) ≥ (1−p̄)r ≥ μ*. At the proposed invariant chain u+v>4, so the hold constraints are feasible. The hub–rim contrast eigenvalue is −1/m, bounded in modulus by μ* (including equality at m=4); the rim modes attain both ±μ*. The same two affine tests give p*−p̄≤ε/r and |q̄−q*|≤H. The first-mode Rayleigh quotient is at least μ*−(u/v)ε. For M=μ(P)I−(P−J) one has 0≤M≤2μ(P)I, so ||Mf||²≤2μ(P)⟨f,Mf⟩ and ||(P−P*)f||≤B. Dividing by f_j on the rim gives imaginary part sin(2π/m)(δq_j−δq_{j−1}); the cycle spectral gap is 4 sin²(π/m), yielding (1). The real part gives the spoke bound (2) by the triangle inequality, with coefficient 2(1−cos(2π/m))=u. Both bounds vanish at ε=0, and the row sums fix the holding weights. value.rationale: The established minimum alone would not tell whether noisy, asymmetric edge assignments can remain optimal. The theorem rules out that ambiguity and provides explicit bounds on individual edge families from observable spectral suboptimality.
